subtype: Approach: mock tests followed by error analysis [Action]
passage: Every Sunday at 9, Joseph sat at the table on the verandah of his family's house in Thrissur and took a full three-hour mock for the railway recruitment exam. His friend Pranav, preparing for the same exam, came over after lunch to check answers with him. Then came the part Joseph liked most: sorting. Every wrong answer went into one of three columns on a sheet. Concept gap: didn't know it. Silly error: knew it, marked the wrong option. Time: never reached it. This week: concept gaps 6, silly errors 11, time 4. "Eleven silly ones," Pranav said. "That's the biggest." Joseph nodded. "So this week isn't new chapters. It's slowing down. I'll underline the key word in each question and check every calculation once." The next Sunday, silly errors fell to five.

qa.q: How many silly errors were there this week?
How does Joseph feel about the sorting?
qa.a: Joseph enjoys it, finding it the part he likes most, since it shows exactly where marks are lost.

qa.q: What else could Joseph track over several Sundays?
qa.a: He could chart the three counts week after week, to see which kind of error is shrinking and which needs attention next.

qa.q: How does Pranav help the process?
qa.a: Pranav checks the answers with Joseph and points out the largest column, which helps focus the next week.

grounding: Shows an aspirant taking a full mock every Sunday, sorting wrong answers into concept gaps, silly errors and time problems, and planning around the largest.

subtype: Approach: mock tests followed by error analysis [Action]
passage: In Kaito's small apartment in Osaka, Sunday mornings belonged to the mock exam. Three hours, phone in the other room, kitchen timer on the desk. His friend Jin, preparing for the same national certification exam, did the same across town, and at 2 pm they called each other. First the scores, then the real work. Kaito read out his wrong answers and sorted them aloud: "Question 14, never learned that law: concept gap. Question 22, misread 'not': careless. Questions 58 to 60, ran out of time." This week the tally was concept gaps 9, careless 4, time 7. "Concepts are biggest," Jin said. "So next week, two new chapters and fewer practice sets?" Kaito wrote the plan on the whiteboard: labour law and contracts, three days each. He also set a rule for the time problem: move on after ninety seconds.

qa.q: What time did Kaito and Jin call each other?
How does Kaito seem to feel about sorting mistakes aloud?
qa.a: Kaito seems calm and focused, treating wrong answers as useful information rather than something to feel bad about.

qa.q: What else could Kaito do about the time problems?
qa.a: Kaito could practise short timed sections midweek, so pacing improves alongside the new chapters.

qa.q: How does Jin's weekly call help Kaito?
qa.a: Jin gives a regular partner to review with and helps name the biggest category, making the next week's plan clearer.

grounding: Illustrates an aspirant taking a weekly mock, sorting errors into concept, careless and time categories, and planning the next week around the largest.
